subject.title: Feature request: native Codex quota/auth diagnosis plus brokered reauth execution

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider/Gateway recovery contract and a brokered host-side reauth execution boundary for Codex OAuth failures?
rationale: The remaining work is not just implementation: it decides which auth states are core API, what UI/channel surfaces may trigger recovery, and what host-side OAuth execution boundary is safe.

options.title: Approve typed diagnosis first
options.body: Add the quota_wait versus reauth_required contract and UI/channel messaging now, while treating brokered execution as a separately reviewed security boundary.

options.title: Keep brokered execution outside core
options.body: Implement only core diagnosis/display and require brokered reauth to live in a plugin or deployment-specific adapter until a stable extension API is approved.

options.title: Decline brokered reauth
options.body: Keep explicit /login codex and operator guidance as the supported recovery path, and close the broker portion as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Approve typed diagnosis first
recommendation.body: Add the quota_wait versus reauth_required contract and UI/channel messaging now, while treating brokered execution as a separately reviewed security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider usage, UX, security posture, and core/plugin boundaries where this owner has recent adjacent history.
